context.snippet: www.barchart.com A Closer Look at Meta's Q2 Earnings Report Meta Platforms' fiscal 2026 second-quarter results delivered a mixed bag for investors. The company reported earnings on July 29, and while revenue comfortably beat Wall Street expectations, soaring costs and massive AI-related investments weighed on profitability, sending the stock down 8% in the following trading session. In the second quarter, Meta generated $60.80 billion in revenue, up 28% year-over-year (YOY) and ahead of Wall Street's $60.21 billion forecast. The strong top-line performance was largely powered by continued demand for digital advertising across Meta's Family of Apps. The company's enormous user base also kept growing, with Family daily active people (DAP) averaging 3.60 billion in June, up 3% YOY. Meanwhile, ad impressions delivered across the Family of Apps jumped 14%, while the average price per ad rose 12% from a year earlier, highlighting the continued strength of Meta's advertising engine. However, the picture changed sharply further down the income statement. Total costs and expenses surged 55% YOY to $42.03 billion, putting significant pressure on profitability. The increase was partly driven by $2.4 billion in legal proceeding charges and $1.18 billion in severance costs tied to workforce layoffs. As a result, Meta's operating margin plunged to 31% from 43% in the year-ago quarter. EPS also came under pressure, landing at $6.18, down 13% from $7.14 in Q2 2025 and below analysts' $7.10 consensus estimate.

The explanation is artificial intelligence. Meta makes its money selling ads across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, apps that reached 3.60 billion people a day on average in the quarter’s final month. Now it’s pouring that ad cash into data centers and a new AI product called Muse. Can the stock hold a premium multiple while the cash cushion thins? The answer depends on whether Muse becomes a business of its own, or just a bigger bill.

### A Machine That Sells More and Charges More

A healthy ad business shows volume and price rising together, and Meta delivered both. Ad impressions across its apps rose 14% year over year in fiscal Q2 2026, and the average price per ad rose 12%. Meta Platforms' (NASDAQ:[**META**](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/META)) revenue grew 28% in fiscal Q2 2026, to $60.80 billion. Free cash flow (operating cash flow minus spending on equipment and finance leases) was $784 million, versus $8,549 million a year earlier.

Advertising revenue reached $59.36 billion, and the Family of Apps segment earned $23.39 billion in operating income. Reality Labs, the virtual and augmented reality unit, lost $4.62 billion.

Expenses climbed 55% to $42.03 billion, and not all of it was AI. The total included $2.40 billion of legal charges and $1.18 billion of severance from layoffs. Operating income fell 8% to $18.78 billion, and operating margin dropped to 31% from 43%. GAAP diluted earnings per share were $6.18, down from $7.14.
Guidance looks ahead: third-quarter revenue of $61 billion to $64 billion, full-year expenses of $165 billion to $169 billion, and capital spending of $130 billion to $145 billion, with 2026 operating income still expected to top 2025's. On Muse, BNP Paribas analyst Nick Jones sees strong early interest, helped by Meta's built-in audience. His open question is whether that curiosity turns into regular use and meaningful revenue.
